title: Runtime 1.22 Launch Brief — Workload-aware batching defaults (fast/standard/cost-efficient)
content:
Owner: Connor O'Brien (Release Train Coordination)
Last reviewed: 2026-04-22
Release: Runtime 1.22
Feature: Workload-aware batching defaults (SLO tiers: fast / standard / cost-efficient)

1) Executive summary
Runtime 1.22 introduces customer-facing, tiered batching defaults that map to three latency SLO tiers (fast, standard, cost-efficient). The runtime will select a batching profile based on tier + workload signals (prompt length buckets, streaming vs non-streaming, concurrency) with an override hierarchy that preserves enterprise/Dedicated control.

This launch brief focuses on:
- Release train timing and branch/cut plan
- Dependencies across runtime, perf tooling, observability, docs, SDKs, and Console
- Rollout strategy (internal canary → Hosted subset → Dedicated opt-in → broader default)
- Go/no-go gates and rollback / kill-switch ownership
- External comms readiness checklist and what we will / won’t promise

2) What ships in Runtime 1.22 (in-scope)
Runtime behavior and config surface:
- Three SLO-tier batching profiles (fast/standard/cost-efficient) with safe defaults per supported model families.
- Workload-aware selection inputs: streaming flag, prompt-length buckets, and concurrency signals.
- Tail latency protections for fast tier: tighter wait budget, admission control, anti-starvation tweaks.
- Throughput tuning for cost-efficient tier: more aggressive batching with queue guardrails (avoid queue blowups under burst).
- Profile selection reason codes emitted via metrics/tracing.
- Feature flagging for staged enablement and immediate kill switch.

Observability/tooling:
- Tier labels added to key latency/cost metrics with cardinality controls.
- Dashboards/panels for per-tier latency histograms, queue depth, batch distribution, and regression indicators.
- Perf canary gating on tier-specific SLOs (fast p99 and standard p95 for top models/regions).

Out of scope / explicitly not promised for 1.22
- Real-time per-tenant auto-tuning (we provide recommendations + workload-aware heuristics only).
- Cross-region routing changes beyond existing smart routing policies.
- New model onboarding or broad quantization policy changes beyond compatibility constraints already documented.

3) Release train timeline (target dates)
Note: dates reflect the coordinated cut + staged rollout schedule, not necessarily customer-visible release notes publish date.

3.1 Milestones
- 2026-03-20: Code complete target for runtime scheduler/config changes (all core PRs merged to main).
- 2026-03-24: Perf suite updates complete; mixed workload scenarios landed in benchmark-lab.
- 2026-03-27: Perf canary gating enabled (initially non-blocking, “warn only”).
- 2026-03-31: Runtime 1.22 branch cut.
- 2026-04-02: Release candidate (RC1) built and deployed to internal canary fleet.
- 2026-04-07: Perf canary gating flipped to blocking for protected paths.
- 2026-04-10: Hosted API limited rollout begins (subset of traffic + allowlist).
- 2026-04-15: Dedicated opt-in available (per-tenant/cluster overrides confirmed).
- 2026-04-22: Docs + SDKs + examples confirmed merged; comms readiness review.
- 2026-04-29: Broader Hosted API default expansion (if gates remain green).

3.2 Branch/cut policy
- Runtime 1.22 is cut from main on 2026-03-31.
- Only approved backports allowed after cut (SRE + runtime lead signoff).
- Any change impacting scheduling heuristics, admission control, or metric dimensions requires perf canary pass + SRE acknowledgement.

4) Required dependencies (must be green before expanding rollout)

- Dedicated override precedence: redwood/pr-28503

4.2 Tooling PRs

4.3 Docs/SDKs/examples

6) Rollout plan (feature flag strategy)
High-level: feature is shipped in runtime, but enabled via feature flags and policy configuration.

6.1 Stages
Stage 0 — Internal canary (required)
- Fleet: internal endpoints + employee traffic + synthetic load.
- Goals: validate correctness, reason codes, dashboard integrity, and ensure no metrics cardinality explosion.
- Abort triggers: sustained p99 regression > gate thresholds on fast tier; repeated overload shedding in non-overload conditions; telemetry cost spike beyond budget.

Stage 1 — Hosted API limited rollout
- Enable for an allowlisted subset of routes/models/regions.
- Maintain quick rollback via kill switch (global disable) + per-route disable.
- Monitor support tickets and customer feedback loops (esp. streaming workloads).

Stage 2 — Dedicated opt-in
- Explicit opt-in per tenant/cluster; validate precedence: customer override > route policy > tier default.
- Ensure Dedicated capacity variability and autoscaling guardrails are compatible.

Stage 3 — Broader Hosted default expansion
- Expand percentage gradually with automated safeguards.
- Keep opt-out and per-route overrides available.

6.2 Kill switch and rollback
- Kill switch owner: Rafael Mendes (SRE)
- Runtime config owner: Sofia Ivanova
- Rollback options (in order of preference):
  1) Disable tiered defaults via global flag; revert to previous batching behavior.
  2) Force standard tier only (if fast tier is the only regressor) or cap cost-efficient aggressiveness.
  3) Per-region/per-model disable if regression is localized.
  4) Runtime rollback only if required for correctness (avoid unless severe).

7) Go/No-Go gates
A launch stage cannot expand unless ALL items in the corresponding section are green.

7.1 Perf gates
- perf-canary pass for top model families across primary regions:
  - fast tier p99 within target thresholds
  - standard tier p95 within target thresholds
- No sustained queue depth growth indicating unstable batching under mixed workloads.
- No starvation events in mixed prompt-length scenarios.

7.2 Reliability gates
- Error budget impact acceptable (SRE signoff).
- Overload behavior predictable: backpressure/load shedding consistent with tier policy.
- Alerting tuned to avoid noisy paging while still catching true regressions.

7.3 Observability gates
- Dashboards show tier dimension correctly; reason code metrics present.
- Metric cardinality controls validated (no runaway label explosion).
- Traces sampling decisions confirmed for high-traffic endpoints.

7.4 Product/support readiness gates
- Docs merged and published; SDKs released (or release notes published with availability date if not same-day).
- Support playbook updated: how to force fast tier for streaming, how to verify effective tier, how to interpret reason codes.
- Dedicated override precedence documented with examples.

8) External comms readiness checklist (Hosted + Dedicated)
This is the minimum bar for “publicly mentionable” behavior changes.

8.1 What we will say
- We now offer three batching tiers aligned to customer-facing latency goals.
- Defaults are workload-aware and safer than manual knobs for most workloads.
- Customers can choose/override tier at route/policy level; Dedicated can enforce tenant/cluster overrides.
- We provide observability: per-tier latency/cost breakdown and explainability via reason codes.

8.2 What we will NOT say
- We do not promise universal cost reduction for every workload.
- We do not claim per-tenant auto-tuning or guaranteed optimality.
- We do not claim tier selection changes data handling, logging, or retention (it does not).

9) Known risks + mitigations
Risk: Fast tier p99 regression on specific model family / region
- Mitigation: fast tier admission control + wait budget; ability to force standard tier for affected model/region; per-model disable.

Risk: Metric cardinality / telemetry cost blow-up
- Mitigation: tier labels only on limited metric set; cardinality controls and sampling; hotfix path (pr-28544).

Risk: Starvation under mixed workloads (long prompts + streaming)
- Mitigation: anti-starvation tweaks; mixed workload perf suite scenarios; monitor queue fairness metrics.

Risk: Dedicated override confusion / precedence bugs
- Mitigation: precedence tests; Dedicated opt-in only until support + docs validate; explicit “effective tier” surfaced.

10) Final cut criteria (what makes the train)
Mandatory for Runtime 1.22:
- Feature flag + kill switch in place
- Reason codes emitted
- perf-canary gating enabled and passing
- Dashboards live with tier breakdown

Nice-to-have (can slip if needed, but must be tracked):
- Additional model family profile tuning beyond top 3 families
- Console UX polish beyond minimum “effective tier” display
